text: This is Almond-fastloop, a browser agent that reads the page instead of screenshots, and decides every step in a quarter of a second.
We are about to run it through the Browser Use Olympics: a benchmark with five events, one server-side clock, and one prompt, visit this page and follow the instructions.
The page carries the tasks: fill a form, find one link among sixteen, carry a code across pages, reach a hidden button, and leave a red button alone.
Before the clock starts, the loop reads the instructions once and plans. Then every action comes from TypeSafe's Jev, a decision model that picks from the buttons and fields actually on the page.
No screenshots, no frontier model in the loop, nothing to hallucinate from. The clock starts the moment it presses Start run.
Watch the pace: the form, the link, the relay code read on one page and typed on the next, each decision a few hundred milliseconds.
The scroll, the dialog, the red button untouched. At the finish it reports its own tokens.
Thirteen point four seconds, five for five, a fifth of a cent. Codex over fifty, Claude sixty-four, Grok two hundred. It is all on the Hall of Fame, and the code is open.
